svg.title: Classification of aggregation functions (based on Pradera et al., 2016)
svg.desc: Accurate, mathematically verified diagram of the classification of aggregation functions (all 57 elementary regions from Tables 8–11) showing the partition into four main classes (Conjunctive, Averaging, Disjunctive, Mixed), conjunctors, disjunctors, semi-copulas, neutral and absorbing elements, zero and one divisors, and non-contradiction and excluded-middle principles.

g.text: ELABORATED ON THE BASIS OF: A. PRADERA, G. BELIAKOV, H. BUSTINCE, B. DE BAETS (2016) · DOI: 10.1016/j.ins.2015.09.033
Classification of Aggregation Functions and Relationships Between Their Properties
Partition into 4 disjoint classes (solid lines) and cross-cutting boundary & divisor classes
min(x, y) ≨ A(x, y) ≨ max(x, y)
CONJUNCTIVE (CONJ): A ≤ min (always satisfies AE(0) and 1Strict)
DISJUNCTIVE (DISJ): A ≥ max (always satisfies AE(1) and 0Strict)
AVERAGING (AVG): min ≨ A ≨ max (idempotent, never 0Div or 1Div)
MIXED: remaining aggregation functions (e.g. uninorms, nullnorms, TS-functions)
Semi-copulas · NE(1): A(x,1) = A(1,x) = x (includes t-norms, copulas)
Dual semi-copulas · NE(0): A(x,0) = A(0,x) = x (includes t-conorms)
2. ZERO/ONE DIVISORS, NC & EM PRINCIPLES (TABLE 1, DEF. 16)
1Strict (one strict): A(x,y) = 1 ⇒ x = y = 1 (disjoint from AE(1) & 1Div)
0Strict (zero strict): A(x,y) = 0 ⇒ x = y = 0 (disjoint from AE(0) & 0Div)
Disjunctors A vs. generated implications I_A(x,y) = A(1−x, y) (Fig. 3):
• S-EM ⇔ (OP) x ≤ y ⇔ I(x,y)=1 • EM ⇔ (IP) I(x,x)=1

svg.text: 4. N-DUALITY SYMMETRY WITH RESPECT TO A STRONG NEGATION N: A^N(x,y) = N(A(N(x), N(y)))
CONJ (A ≤ min) ⇄ DISJ (A ≥ max) · CONJUNCTORS AE(0) ⇄ DISJUNCTORS AE(1) · Semi-copulas NE(1) ⇄ Dual semi-copulas NE(0)
1Strict ⇄ 0Strict · 0Div ⇄ 1Div · NC(N) ⇄ EM(N) · S-NC(N) ⇄ S-EM(N) · AVG ⇄ AVG (closed under duality) · MIXED ⇄ MIXED (closed)

Elaborated on the basis of: A. Pradera, G. Beliakov, H. Bustince, B. De Baets, "A review of the relationships between implication, negation and aggregation functions from the point of view of material implication", Information Sciences 329 (2016) 357–380, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2015.09.033
